levels.title: The Chicken-Nado
levels.subtitle: The sky is clucking and Dad says this is normal.
levels.inspired: The road trip to Grandma's house, the semi truck, and the buffet we sheltered in.
levels.goal: Find your three memories, poke at the mystery, then face whatever is stirring the mashed potatoes.

boss.name: The Barefoot Buffet Keeper
boss.taunt: You want the buffet? You gotta get past the mashed potatoes. And me. Mostly me.
boss.win: He hands over a crate of chickens and one very buttery spoon.

intro.text: Mile two hundred and twelve. Dad has been singing the same nine words for an hour.
I counted them. It is nine words. It's a very good song.
Kids, look! A tornado! And it is carrying chickens! This is the best road trip of our lives!
Everyone out. We are sheltering in that gas station buffet and we are not discussing it further.

outro.text: The chickens flew the crate all the way to the interstate. That is teamwork.
The Keeper left something behind. A postcard with no picture on it, just the words 'keep this one'.
Buckle up. Grandma's house is only six hours away, which means nine hours.

levels.title: Terror at Bear Cabin Ridge
levels.subtitle: A three-story cabin, a mountain coaster, and something in the basement theater.
levels.inspired: The cabin with the pool table, the shuffleboard, and every noise the woods make at 2 a.m.
levels.goal: Memories are hiding around the cabin. Something is making bird calls that are not birds.

boss.name: The Whoopin' Stick Grandma
boss.taunt: I heard you kids been whoopin' on my stick. Let's see how you slide, sugar.
boss.win: She whoops once, respects it, and leaves a puck on the table for you.

intro.text: The cabin has three floors, a pool table, and a theater in the basement. Dad has already claimed all of it.
A bear looked in the window and waved. I waved back. We're friends now.
That was a decoration. The decorations do not wave. Please stop saying the decorations wave.
Somebody left the shuffleboard set up. And there's a whoopin' stick. That is not a normal cabin item.

outro.text: The bear took the last puck and did not say thank you, which is rude.
Another card. This one says 'bear with me'. It has a tiny photo of our cabin stapled to it.
Who wants to ride the mountain coaster at night? Nobody? Great, everyone's coming!

levels.title: The Prairie Dog-Ferret War
levels.subtitle: Beneath the hills, two tiny nations are one bad rumor from war.
levels.inspired: Wind Cave, the prairie dog towns, and the black-footed ferrets nobody ever actually sees.
levels.goal: The towns suspect you are spies. Find your memories and get down into the caves before the parade starts.

boss.name: The Ferret King
boss.taunt: You have entered the Ferret Kingdom without a form. Nobody enters without a form!
boss.win: The King stamps your form, gives you a crown, and immediately requests it back.

intro.text: The prairie dogs have a mayor. He has a tiny hat. I would follow him anywhere.
They think we're ferret spies. The ferrets think we're prairie dog spies. We are nine and seven.
I once lost a staring contest to a prairie dog. Not my proudest moment. Anyway, let's go underground!
Wind Cave has sixty-five miles of passages. We are not exploring sixty-five miles. We are exploring four.

outro.text: The parade was mostly one guy and a very confident sign. Ten out of ten.
The King's crown had a note in it. 'Every family forgets a little. It's what I'm for.' The handwriting is tiny and sad.
Next stop: a town called Storybook Land. I want to be very clear that I did not choose it.

levels.title: Storybook Land After Dark
levels.subtitle: After closing time, the nursery rhymes get up and stretch.
levels.inspired: The storybook park where the characters were way more alive than advertised.
levels.goal: The Storybook Clock has stopped, and every character is stuck mid-rhyme. Three memories are loose in the park.

boss.name: The Keeper's Hour Hand
boss.taunt: Tick. Tock. You are late for a bedtime that happened forty years ago.
boss.win: The clock chimes seven, the rhymes finish themselves, and the whole park exhales.

intro.text: The giant sheep let me pet it. Then it followed me. Then it followed me into the gift shop.
The characters are all frozen in the middle of their rhymes. The clock stopped at seven. It's not seven.
I have always wanted to fix a giant clock at night with zero qualifications. Dream big, kids.
There is a pumpkin looking at us. I am going to need everyone to be calm and nobody to scream.

outro.text: The sheep said goodbye. It sounded like a truck.
There was a page tucked in the clock. It's from our scrapbook. It's a picture of this exact night, taken before we got here.
Kansas City! Union Station! Science City! The Rabbit Hole! I have made a schedule and it is already wrong!

levels.title: The Kansas City Conspiracy
levels.subtitle: A machine is mixing science experiments with fairy tales, and the rabbit is not sorry.
levels.inspired: Union Station, Science City, and the Rabbit Hole where nothing made sense on purpose.
levels.goal: The Mad Inventor Rabbit has wired the exhibits into something impossible. Find the memories and untangle it.

boss.name: The Mad Inventor Rabbit
boss.taunt: You are standing in my laboratory! Which is also a train station! Which is also a fairy tale! Keep up!
boss.win: He admits the machine only ever made one thing: a very complicated apology.

intro.text: The Rabbit Hole has a room where the ceiling is the floor. Mom said 'absolutely not' and then went in first.
I put my hand in the science machine and now my hand is ten minutes in the future.
That's my boy. Science City, everybody. Where the experiments are also a personality test.
Every exhibit is glowing in a pattern. It's not random. It's a beam. Somebody is routing something through this whole building.

outro.text: The rabbit gave me a carrot. It is also a key. It tastes like a key.
The blueprint was signed 'for the family that always comes back'. The ink is the exact color of our scrapbook.
Omaha. The Luminarium. A building full of light and fog. What could possibly go wrong.

levels.title: The Luminarium Dimension
levels.subtitle: A dome made of light, a room made of fog, and a sculpture that has opinions.
levels.inspired: The Luminarium, where light behaves like weather and the fog room eats your family one at a time.
levels.goal: The Living Light Sculpture swallowed the colors. Find your memories and put them back in order.

boss.name: The Living Light Sculpture
boss.taunt: I contain every color your family has ever argued about. Sort them out, if you can.
boss.win: It turns a soft, embarrassed shade of pink and hands over a very small rainbow.

intro.text: I went into the fog room and came out in a different room and possibly a different year.
The lights are all wrong. Not broken. Wrong. Somebody mixed our memories into the color wheel.
This is the most beautiful place I have ever been and I have no idea where your mother is.
I am right here. I have been right here. You are standing on my foot.

outro.text: The sculpture's light landed on a photo. Not ours. A vacation with nobody in it. Empty chairs, set for a family that never came.
That's the saddest picnic I've ever seen.
Last stop. The Pavilion. And then we are going home and nobody is allowed to say the word 'vacation' for a year.

levels.title: Attack of the Pavilion
levels.subtitle: The museum woke up, and it has been waiting for your family.
levels.inspired: The Washington Pavilion, where every exhibit is one closing-time away from a mutiny.
levels.goal: Every exhibit in the building is awake. Find the last three memories and end this.

boss.name: The Vacation Collector
boss.taunt: You always leave. You take one photo and you leave, and the day sits here in the dark getting smaller.
boss.win: It puts down the box. It has never been asked to stay.

intro.text: The dinosaur is awake. The dinosaur is awake and it is doing a little dance.
This is where all the clues were pointing. Somebody has been taking pieces of every vacation we ever took.
Buddy, if a museum wants to fight this family, it should know we have survived nine hours in a minivan.
Jira. Joel. Stay together. Whatever is in there has been alone for a very long time.

outro.text: It wasn't stealing the vacations. It was keeping them. It thought nobody else would.
We told it it could come next time. It fit in the cupholder. Don't ask.
One photo. All four of us. And one very small shadow in the corner, if that's all right.
Best vacation ever. I'm putting it on a mug.
